newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian bond tranche priced at 100.14 pct.
newsitem.headline: Russian bond tranche priced at 100.14 pct.

text.p: The average price of a new 518-day tranche of 18-month OFZ interest-bearing bonds (series 24010) was 100.14 percent at an auction on Wednesday, the Central Bank said.
When the series 24010 bonds were first sold on December 18, the average price was 93.02 percent. The earlier tranche of the 24010 bonds closed on Tuesday at 100.15 percent, yielding 36.26.
At the last auction of OFZ bonds on December 25, a new tranche of the bonds maturing May 28, 1997 (series 24004), was priced at an average 100.17 percent.
Issue volume 3.00 trln rbls 2.00 trln rbls
Earlier the Finance Ministry auctioned 7.50 trillion roubles of 266-day GKO discount Treasury bills, raising 5.37 trillion roubles at an average yield of 33.22 percent.
That takes total proceeds from Wednesday's auctions to 6.81 trillion roubles.

On January 15 the Finance Ministry is also repaying about 6.08 trillion roubles of maturing six-month bills (series 22039), and paying about 582 billion roubles in interest on the two-year OFZ bond (series 24008) maturing July 1998.
The new bills and bonds are subject to the existing tax regime, which frees income from government securities from tax.

President Boris Yeltsin signed a law on Wednesday imposing a 15 percent tax on income from government securities but it has not yet come into force. Securities issued before the tax comes into effect will not be taxable.
